prompt: Maya authorizes the coordinator to run the emulator check and to delegate source reading. A helper needs the controller and adapter definitions to compare their wording. Which handoff fits the grant?

options.text: Lend the helper the coordinator’s credentials for the time needed to finish the comparison.
options.feedback: The borrowed credentials also allow test execution. A later reviewer would see the coordinator’s identity on reads made by the helper.

options.text: Give the helper its own identity and read access to the two specified revisions. Link the handoff to Maya’s grant.
options.feedback: The helper has the access it needs, and Maya can trace which agent read which definitions under her authorization.

options.text: Let the helper edit either definition when the two owners have used different words for the same field.
options.feedback: Rewriting a definition could change the meaning of acknowledgment. The interface owners need to review that proposed change.

prompt: Suppose the runner stops before the software check starts. The allowed retry then reports “indication confirmed” for an amber request with only a receipt. What should the coordinator do next?

options.text: Keep the interrupted attempt and the completed retry. Return the unexpected display text with the command, inputs, test revision and configuration.
options.feedback: The first attempt produced no test result. The retry exposed a discrepancy against the agreed display criterion. The owners can now inspect it on the same configuration.

options.text: Keep retrying until the runner reports “indication unknown,” then hand over the most recent result.
options.feedback: The grant covers one retry after a runner failure. A completed check that reports unexpected behavior gives the team an engineering finding worth retaining.

options.text: Update the expected text to “indication confirmed,” since revision B promises an acknowledgment for that request.
options.feedback: Revision B promises receipt. Using that promise as the expected indication would repeat the assumption the test was intended to challenge.

prompt: The team is considering a later adapter revision C that changes when it sends confirmation. Maya has the deferred A/B decision and the planned bench procedure. What would let her assess compatibility for A/C?

options.text: Reuse the A/B disposition because the controller is still revision A and the same person owns the decision.
options.feedback: The decision owner and controller are unchanged, but the adapter now asserts something different. The A/B record explains the earlier decision and the evidence it lacked.

options.text: Accept A/C when a properly authorized reviewer checks that the evaluation log conforms to the expected schema.
options.feedback: The reviewer could establish that the log has the required structure. Maya would still need the meaning of C’s confirmation and evidence of what the head displayed.

options.text: Have the owners agree on C’s confirmation and fault behavior, run the independent observation on the identified A/C configuration, and take those records to Maya.
options.feedback: This gives Maya the proposed contract and relevant observations for the new pair. She can decide what the evidence supports and record any remaining limits.
